newsitem.title: FRANCE: French train strike hits services.
newsitem.headline: French train strike hits services.

text.p: A strike by train conductors over wages and working conditions cut rail services to about a third of normal in many parts of France on Thursday, state-run SNCF railways said.

SNCF said Eurostar trains linking Paris and London via the Channel tunnel and most suburban services around Paris were the only ones to escape disruption by the strike by 10,000 conductors, between 8 p.m. on Wednesday and 8 a.m. on Friday.
Express and regional services in other parts of the country were cut to about a third of normal. Two out of three high speed trains between Paris and Brussels were running normally.

Six trade unions called the strike to urge wage hikes and protest conditions, a new sign of labour unrest and opposition to austerity measures amid campaigning for a snap parliamentary election for May 25-June 1.
Trains cannot run without the conductors because they are responsible for safety aboard trains as well as checking tickets.

Meanwhile, a delegation of striking fishermen blockading the northern ports of Dunkirk, Calais and Boulogne despite a court injuction was due to meet Agriculture Minister Philippe Vasseur over their demands on Thursday morning.

The fishermen are protesting at European Union regulations calling for bigger holes in the mesh of their nets. Their action has left hundreds of trucks blocking the motorway on the British side of the Channel leading to the port of Dover.
French courts on Wednesday granted European ferry giants P&O, Stena Line AB, and Sea France an injunction to lift the blockade, begun on Tuesday.
